_readme: THE IARC AGE-RATING ANSWERS — Nikatru Subscription Tracker, channel `windows-store`.
🔴 THIS FILE RECORDS ANSWERS. IT DOES NOT RECORD A RATING, AND IT MUST NOT. Partner Center's age
ratings step is the IARC questionnaire: the developer answers and the rating authorities assign the
ratings. `assignedRating` is therefore null and `status` says why, exactly as in
android-play/content-rating.json and ios-appstore/age-rating.json, for the same reason they give.
WHY IT EXISTS (O-WINDOWS-AGE-RATING-ANSWERS-UNRECORDED): until 2026-10-01 these answers existed nowhere
in the repository. Only the declaration DATE was gated (apps/subscriptiontracker/app.yaml
`stores.windows-store.declaredOn`, tooling/ci/submit-preconditions.mjs), so the owner would have typed
the questionnaire from memory at the first Partner Center submission.
DERIVED, NOT RE-MEASURED. IARC is ONE questionnaire behind both storefronts, and this is one app with
one set of behaviours. So every claim below carries `fromPlayClaim`, the id of the
android-play/content-rating.json claim it is derived from, and tooling/ci/assert-store-audience.mjs
FAILS if an answer differs from that claim's, if a Play claim has no Windows row, or if a row names
no Play claim. A second measurement of the same behaviour is how two answers to one question drift.
Where a claim's evidence on Windows differs from Play's, the `note` says how.
⚠️ THE PARTNER CENTER WORDING IS UNVERIFIED — see `questionnaireWording`. The Partner Center account
cannot authenticate yet (no Entra tenant, O-MSSTORE-ENTRA-TENANT), so the questionnaire has not been
opened. When it is, map each question onto a claim; a question that maps onto none is a missing row
here AND on Play, because the two claim sets are held equal.
HAND-OWNED. [ADR 037]: "a sworn declaration regenerated by a template is a statement nobody made."
tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs must never write this file.
⚠️ NOT LEGAL ADVICE AND NOT WRITTEN BY A LAWYER, the same disclaimer tooling/legal/README.md carries.
statusReason: The Partner Center age ratings questionnaire has not been submitted: the account has no Entra tenant and cannot authenticate (O-MSSTORE-ENTRA-TENANT), and `declaredOn` is null for this channel in apps/subscriptiontracker/app.yaml. Until it is submitted there is no rating and no IARC certificate. The answers below are prepared; submitting them is a per-app Partner Center action, and publishing is the owner's word alone (C-MANUAL-FIRST-PUBLISH).

derivedFrom.rule: every claim here equals the claim of the same id there (`fromPlayClaim`), and the two claim sets are the same set
derivedFrom.why: IARC (the International Age Rating Coalition) issues ratings for both Google Play and the Microsoft Store from one questionnaire. Answering it twice from two measurements of one app is how the two answers come to disagree.

audienceFloor.source: [ADR 068] — no NIKATRU app, extension or site targets children; the audience floor is 18
audienceFloor.consequence: Every answer below is consistent with an adult-only audience; `target-audience-children` answers false, and tooling/ci/assert-store-audience.mjs pins both that answer and this floor.

questionnaireWording.why: Partner Center renders the IARC questionnaire inside the product's Age ratings page after sign-in, and this account cannot sign in yet (no Entra tenant). No question text is reproduced here, because plausible wording would make this file look like a filled-in form while being a guess about someone else's UI.
questionnaireWording.consequence: The claims are about the APP, not about the form. Mapping them onto Partner Center's actual questions is a human step, and `humanOwned.mapClaimsToPartnerCenterQuestions` records it as one.

claims.claim: The app is an application, not a game. The questionnaire branches on this at the first question and the whole downstream question set differs.
claims.note: Partner Center lists the app under Productivity (store/windows-store/category.txt), as Play does; IARC branches on app-vs-game at its first question on every storefront.

claims.claim: The app offers digital purchases: its own premium subscription, presented in-app, with purchase execution OFF-DEVICE on the apex web checkout ([ADR 038]).
claims.note: On Windows the purchase rail is the third-party one Microsoft Store Policies §10.8.1/§10.8.6 permit (packages/purchases/lib/src/purchase_capabilities.dart, [ADR 039]); it is still a digital purchase of the app's own subscription, which is what the IARC question asks.

claims.claim: The app contains no advertising of any kind, and no advertising or attribution SDK.
claims.note: The same binary set of behaviours as Play: no ads SDK, no house ad. android-play/ads-declaration.json is the format-keyed derivation and tooling/ci/assert-ads-declarations.mjs holds it to the tree.

claims.claim: The app does not generate content with AI: no text, image, voice or video is produced by a model for the user.
claims.note: apps/subscriptiontracker/app.yaml `ai.generatesContent: false`; the Play claim's tells are the guard on it.

claims.claim: The app contains no gambling, simulated gambling, loot boxes, or real-money wagering.
claims.note: No chance mechanic and no wagering surface on any platform; the Play claim's tells are the guard on it.

claims.claim: Users cannot interact with, message, or exchange content with other users. There is no social surface.
claims.note: Single-user by construction on every platform: one API, every route scoped to the caller's own rows.

claims.claim: The app does not share a user's physical location with other users.
claims.note: The app never obtains a location on any platform, and has no user-to-user surface to share one on.

claims.claim: The app does not share personal information with third parties.
claims.note: One Data safety inventory describes the one backend every platform calls; the Play claim cross-checks it.

claims.claim: The app is not designed for or targeted at children.
claims.note: [ADR 068]: the audience floor is 18 on every channel. tooling/ci/assert-store-audience.mjs pins this answer to false here and on Play.

claims.claim: The app contains no violence, sexual content, nudity, profanity, crude humour, horror, or references to drugs, alcohol or tobacco.
claims.note: HUMAN-OWNED on Play and therefore here: the Windows listing copy and screenshots (store/windows-store/) join the surfaces a person re-reads before affirming it.

sources: apps/subscriptiontracker/store/android-play/content-rating.json — the claims these are derived from, and the IARC sources it cites
[ADR 068] no NIKATRU app targets children; audience floor 18
[ADR 037] a sworn declaration regenerated by a template is a statement nobody made
[ADR 039] the Windows purchase rail, declared in Partner Center
apps/subscriptiontracker/app.yaml — `stores.windows-store`: the record this declaration belongs to and its `declaredOn` date
tooling/ci/submit-preconditions.mjs — DECLARATION_ONLY_CHANNELS: the date gate a real Windows submission passes
tooling/ci/assert-sworn-store-files.mjs — the floors that keep this file answered rather than drifting back to the stamp

humanOwned._why: What a repository cannot do for this form, named so it is visible rather than hidden inside a claim that looks checked.
humanOwned.mapClaimsToPartnerCenterQuestions: When the Partner Center questionnaire is opened, match each question to one or more claims above. A question matching none means this file AND android-play/content-rating.json are missing a row, and both grow it before either form is submitted.
humanOwned.affirmContentDescriptors: The `content-descriptors` claim is human-owned on Play; a person re-reads the Windows listing copy and screenshots (apps/subscriptiontracker/store/windows-store/) as well as the Play surfaces before affirming it.
humanOwned.recordTheOutcome: When the questionnaire is submitted, the IARC certificate id and the per-authority ratings go into `assignedRating` WITH a source, and the date into app.yaml `stores.windows-store.declaredOn`. Until then both stay null.
